title: Not good to be alone (Genesis 2:18–25)
hook: the only thing in creation God calls not good is loneliness

segments.voice: Yesterday, dust and breath: clay on a workbench and God's breath, face to face. Your line was dust that breathes. When did you feel both halves? A new week starts. Day three hundred thirty-seven.

Count the verdicts so far. Light: good. Dry land and sea: good. Plants: good. Sun, moon and stars: good. Fish and birds, cattle and creeping things: good. Everything together: very good. Genesis keeps saying it like a bell. And then, in the garden, with the first human freshly made and a whole world to tend, the bell rings wrong. God looks at the man and says something is not good. Not sin. Nothing has gone wrong yet. No serpent, no fruit. Just one person, by himself, in paradise.
screen: `GOOD, GOOD, GOOD, VERY GOOD.` → `THE BELL RINGS WRONG.` → `ONE PERSON, BY HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: Here's the line in the Douay-Rheims: "It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself." First, the problem. The first thing in the Bible called not good isn't evil. It's being alone. The man has God, a garden and work, and still something is missing. Second, the word help. In Hebrew it's ezer kenegdo, a helper corresponding to him, one who stands facing him. Ezer is not a servant's word. The Hebrew Bible uses it most often for God, who is Israel's help. So the help God promises isn't an assistant. It's a partner, an equal, someone who can look back. Third, the search. God brings the animals to the man, and he names every one. Cattle, birds, beasts of the field. But none of them is the help like himself. Then God casts the man into a deep sleep, takes one of his ribs, closes up the flesh, and builds a woman. When he wakes and sees her, the first human words in the Bible spill out, and they're close to a song: this now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. Fourth, how the Church reads it. The Catechism says man and woman are made for each other, a communion of persons, and that this is where marriage begins. But the Church also reads the line more widely: no human being is made to be alone. Friendship, family, parish, neighbors: all of them answer the same not good. And the garden scene ends quietly. They were both naked, and were not ashamed.
screen: `THE FIRST NOT GOOD: ALONE.` · `EZER: A HELP, LIKE GOD IS.` · `NO ANIMAL IS LIKE HIMSELF.` · `BONE OF MY BONES.` · then, large: `IT IS NOT GOOD FOR MAN TO BE ALONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: reach out to someone alone. Settle, and breathe. Let a face come to mind: someone living by themselves, a widower down the street, a friend who moved to a new city, a coworker who eats lunch at the desk, an older relative whose phone doesn't ring much. Stay with that one person. Picture where they are right now, what the room sounds like. If you pray, you can hold them before God by name. After the bell, send one message or make one call. Nothing big. Just proof that someone thought of them. The bell holds the time.
Not good to be alone. The first not good in the Bible: one person, by himself. God's answer is a help like himself, an equal who stands facing him.
screen: `NOT GOOD TO BE ALONE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: not good to be alone. Today, notice who's on the edge of the room, the group chat or the table, and pull them one step in. Day three hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Genesis 2:18–24 is one of the Old Testament readings Catholic couples can choose for their wedding Mass, and the Church reads it as the beginning of marriage and of all human community.

original.note: Hebrew: a help corresponding to him, standing facing him. ezer is often used of God.

trapdoor: what you thought: the woman was made as an assistant.
what it means: God's answer to loneliness is an equal, a partner who stands facing him.
what a scholar hears: ezer kenegdo; ezer is used most often of God as Israel's helper, and kenegdo means corresponding to, opposite.

sources.quoted: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself.

notes: 'The first thing called not good' follows the index; confirm.
ezer used most often of God (e.g. Psalm 120/121:1–2, Psalm 32/33:20); confirm 'most often'.
'Bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh' (2:23) given as paraphrase without quotation marks; Douay-Rheims reads 'This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh'. Could be quoted once confirmed.
CCC 371–372 (man and woman made for each other, communion of persons), CCC 1605 (marriage). Paraphrased; confirm.
